Definition: from G1909 and a derivative of G3717; to straighten further, i.e. (figuratively) arrange additionally:--set in order.
BiblicalUsage: Epidiorthoo means to set in order what remains — to straighten further. Paul left Titus in Crete to set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as he had appointed him.
TheologicalSignificance: Paul did not leave Crete half-ordered, and the church still needs men who will set in order what remains.
